edge_claim: The pre-coup constitutional order preserved institutional autonomy and political power for the military, creating capacity for intervention during the post-election rupture.
mechanism: Reserved constitutional authority, control of coercive institutions and institutional autonomy reduced civilian control over the armed forces.
alternative_interpretations: Military autonomy existed before earlier elections without producing a coup each time.

edge_claim: Decades of military-dominated governance contributed to the institutional position retained by the armed forces in the pre-2021 constitutional order.
mechanism: Long-run control of state institutions shaped organizational autonomy, political expectations and coercive capacity.
alternative_interpretations: The 2008 constitutional system also represented a partial transition and differed materially from earlier military regimes.

edge_claim: Long-running center-periphery conflicts became embedded in borderland political economies and cross-border networks that affected armed actors' capacities.
mechanism: Territorial control, trade routes and border economies provided channels for taxation, commerce, sanctuary and resource movement.
alternative_interpretations: Different ethnic armed organizations have distinct territorial, political and economic systems.

edge_claim: Conflict-resource economies provided material support to some state and non-state armed actors within long-running armed conflicts.
mechanism: Resource extraction, taxation, concessions and commercial networks generated revenue or material capacity for specific actors.
alternative_interpretations: Resource income does not establish political motive and is uneven across organizations and regions.

edge_claim: The absence of a durable federal settlement after independence contributed to a political environment in which center-periphery disputes repeatedly became armed conflicts.
mechanism: Unresolved authority, autonomy and territorial questions persisted through changing regimes and created recurrent bargaining and conflict structures.
alternative_interpretations: Each later conflict has distinct local actors and causes; continuity cannot be assumed uniformly.

edge_claim: Colonial administrative and territorial arrangements may have shaped some of the institutional and center-periphery problems inherited at independence.
mechanism: Different administrative regimes, territorial classifications and political institutions affected the conditions under which the post-colonial state was assembled.
alternative_interpretations: Pre-colonial political structures, wartime changes and post-independence choices may be equally or more important in particular regions.

edge_claim: Regional borderland networks could increase the durability of conflict-resource economies by connecting local extraction and armed control to external markets and routes.
mechanism: Cross-border commerce and logistics can convert territorial/resource control into revenue and supplies.
alternative_interpretations: Some external trade may be ordinary civilian commerce and should not be classified as conflict support without actor-level evidence.

edge_claim: Myanmar entered the 2021 political rupture with an already fragmented coercive landscape, limiting the conflict to neither a simple civilian-versus-military nor purely central-state contest.
mechanism: Existing ethnic armed organizations, territorial control and prior conflicts shaped the actors, safe areas and alliance options available after the coup.
alternative_interpretations: Many new post-coup resistance groups had distinct urban and local origins rather than direct continuity from older ethnic conflicts.
